blocks.orig: Tanzania Safari: Best time of the year ?
blocks.html: Tanzania safari: which time of year is best?

blocks.orig: The decision is made: you are going to spend your holiday in Tanzania ! Congratulations, you have made a fantastic choice. You are now wondering when is the best time to go on a Tanzania safari. Our answer is… it depends ! It depends on what you want to see, to do, if you prefer being alone in the national parks or if you like some company from other tourists.
blocks.html: So it is settled: you are off on holiday in Tanzania ! Congratulations on a wonderful choice. The next question on your mind is probably when to go on your Tanzania safari. Our honest answer is… it depends ! It depends on what you hope to see and do, and on whether you prefer having the national parks to yourself or don't mind sharing them with other visitors.

blocks.orig: Many people say that the best time to visit Tanzania is the dry season, from June to October, or during our winter from December to March. But according to us, there is no such thing as a bad time for your Tanzania safari: when to go to Tanzania depends on your preferences.
blocks.html: You will often hear that the dry season, from June to October, or our winter months from December to March, are the best time to visit Tanzania. In our view, though, there is really no bad time for a Tanzania safari: when you go should come down to what you prefer.

blocks.orig: To help you make a decision on when to visit Tanzania, let’s have a look at the activities, places, and animals you would like to do or see.
blocks.html: To help you decide when to visit Tanzania, let's go through the activities, places and animals you would like to experience.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is located in the Southern Hemisphere. That’s why when it’s summer in England or in the USA, it’s winter in Tanzania! The different seasons in Tanzania are: the dry season, the short rainy season, a new dry and hot season and finally, a long rainy season.
blocks.html: Tanzania sits in the Southern Hemisphere. So when it’s summer in England or the USA, it’s winter in Tanzania! The country’s seasons run as follows: a dry season, a short rainy season, another dry and hot season, and lastly a long rainy season.

blocks.orig: From June to October, it’s winter in Tanzania, we call it the dry season. It hardly ever rains, and the temperatures are pleasant. The weather is warm, but you don’t suffer from the heat.
blocks.html: Between June and October Tanzania has its winter, known as the dry season. Rain is very rare and the temperatures are agreeable: warm, but never oppressively hot.

blocks.orig: often takes place in November and early December. It’s summer in Tanzania, and it’s getting very hot. It rains especially at the end of the day, but it does not rain as hard as during the long rainy season from March to May. The advantage of going to a safari in Tanzania during the short rainy season? Fewer tourists and amazing colors.
blocks.html: usually falls in November and early December. It’s summer in Tanzania by then, and it’s getting very hot. Showers tend to come late in the day, and they are lighter than during the long rains from March to May. Why go on a Tanzania safari in the short rainy season? Fewer visitors and wonderful colours.

blocks.orig: runs from December to February. It can be hot, very hot, especially towards the coast. It hardly rains. Not advised if you generally suffer from the heat.
blocks.html: lasts from December to February. It can be hot, even very hot, particularly near the coast, and there is hardly any rain. Best avoided if heat tends to bother you.

blocks.orig: runs from March to May. It rains often, and it is a bit less warm, but this, in my opinion, not a reason not to visit Tanzania at that time of the year. Indeed, you are almost alone on the roads, as most tourists do not come during this time of the year ! Another very important reason to visit Tanzania during the rainy season is that you also have more chances to see zebra and wildebeest in the Serengeti National Park. Some parks are difficult to access because of the rains, but our guides know where to go! If you love adventure and authenticity: Tanzanian nature is beautiful during the rainy season.
blocks.html: lasts from March to May. Rain is frequent and it is slightly cooler, but to my mind that is no reason to skip Tanzania at this time of year. You will have the roads almost entirely to yourself, since most tourists stay away in these months ! Another strong argument for visiting Tanzania in the rainy season is that your chances of seeing zebra and wildebeest in the Serengeti National Park are better. The rains make some parks hard to reach, but our guides know exactly where to go! If adventure and authenticity appeal to you: Tanzanian nature is at its loveliest in the rainy season.

blocks.orig: You can observe birds the whole year, but you will probably see more birds during the rainy season.
blocks.html: Birdwatching is possible throughout the year, though you are likely to spot more birds in the rainy season.

blocks.orig: Tanzania safari: best Time for animals and nature
blocks.html: Tanzania safari: the best time for wildlife and nature

blocks.orig: Going on a Tanzania safari is possible all year round. You will just not see the same animals and the landscapes will look different.
blocks.html: A Tanzania safari can be done at any time of year. The difference is which animals you see and how the landscapes look.

blocks.orig: We often hear that the rainy season is not the best time to visit Tanzania, but it is not true. On the contrary, the rainy season is when nature is the most beautiful, green and flourishing. Many travelers prefer to go to the northern and central parks (Serengeti among others) in the dry season, between June and October, and from December to February. The weather is nice, but you should know that it is also the peak tourist season: prices and occupancy rates of hotels, lodges, and camps are high.
blocks.html: People often tell us the rainy season is a poor time to visit Tanzania, but that is simply not the case. If anything, this is when nature is at its greenest, lushest and most beautiful. Many travellers choose the northern and central parks (the Serengeti among them) in the dry season, from June to October and from December to February. The weather is lovely then, but be aware that it is also peak tourist season: prices and occupancy at hotels, lodges and camps are high.

blocks.orig: You can dive and snorkel in Tanzania all year ! To go swimming, we often recommend going in January and February, or during the Tanzanian winter, in July and August. The rainy season is also raging on the coast and storms happen regularly, that’s why the rainy season is not the most popular time for diving.
blocks.html: Diving and snorkelling are possible in Tanzania throughout the year ! For swimming, we usually suggest January and February, or the Tanzanian winter in July and August. The rainy season hits the coast hard too, with regular storms, which is why it is the least popular period for diving.

blocks.orig: The best time to visit Tanzania Zanzibar, Pemba and Mafia, is during the Tanzanian winter, between June and September. On the Tanzanian islands, the climate is hot and humid, exceeding 30 degrees during the Tanzanian summer (from December to February). We recommend visiting Zanzibar between June and September, during the dry season. It’s a bit cooler, unless you really enjoy the heat.
blocks.html: If Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia are on your list, the Tanzanian winter from June to September is the time to go. The islands have a hot, humid climate, and in the Tanzanian summer (December to February) the thermometer climbs past 30 degrees. Our suggestion is therefore to see Zanzibar in the dry months, June to September, when it is slightly cooler; unless, of course, heat is exactly what you are after.

blocks.orig: What is the best time of the year to climb Mount Kilimanjaro?
blocks.html: Which time of year is best for climbing Mount Kilimanjaro?

blocks.orig: All year round ! Admittedly, it is less easy at certain times of the year than at others (we think in particular of the rainy season). Note that there are strong temperature differences between the foot and the top of the mountain. Even if it’s hot at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro, it can freeze at the top. February is often considered to be the best time to climb Mount Kilimanjaro. This is one of the hottest months and the temperature at the top is not too cold. If you can not go there in February, know that the whole period from December to February is good to climb on the roof of Africa!
blocks.html: Any time of year ! That said, some periods are harder than others (the rainy season in particular springs to mind). Bear in mind that temperatures differ hugely between the base and the summit: it may be hot at the foot of Mount Kilimanjaro while it’s freezing at the top. February is widely regarded as the best month to climb Mount Kilimanjaro, being one of the warmest months with a summit temperature that is not too severe. If February doesn't work for you, rest assured that the whole stretch from December to February is a good time to climb the roof of Africa!

blocks.orig: Best time for a Tanzania safari – By geographical area
blocks.html: When to go on a Tanzania safari – by region

blocks.orig: There are different types of climates in Tanzania. Of course, you will not have the same weather on the island of Zanzibar, in the Serengeti National Park, as at the top of Mount Kilimanjaro!
blocks.html: Tanzania is home to several distinct climates. Naturally, the conditions you meet on Zanzibar bear little resemblance to those in the Serengeti National Park, let alone at the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro!

blocks.orig: The Tanzanian coast enjoys a humid equatorial climate, where it averages between 25 °C and 30 °C. In contrast, the highlands and inland areas are subject to a temperate tropical climate. In the large parks of the north, the temperatures in the day are pleasant, but do not forget to bring a jacket for the evening because it is cold when the night falls.
blocks.html: Along the coast of Tanzania the climate is humid and equatorial, averaging between 25 °C and 30 °C. The highlands and the interior, by contrast, are temperate tropical. Days in the big northern parks are comfortably warm, but pack a jacket for after dark, because the evenings turn chilly.

blocks.orig: There are several best times to visit Tanzania. Many tourists like to go during dry, sunny seasons from January to March and from July to October. However, if you want to meet fewer people on the road and if you suffer from heat, we advise you to go before or after the dry season in June or September. You will enjoy the great weather without being there during the high season.
blocks.html: In truth there is more than one best time to visit Tanzania. Plenty of tourists favour the dry, sunny periods from January to March and from July to October. But if you would rather share the road with fewer people, or you struggle with heat, our recommendation is to travel just before or after the dry season, in June or September. You get the fine weather without the high-season crowds.
